release_notes.en-US: Flows: an agent can save a task on a site as steps and replay it in one call, including inside embedded frames and shadow DOM. Agents can click at a point in a screenshot, which makes canvas apps usable. The network log now shows fetch and XHR response bodies in Firefox, and console output from the first moments of a page load is captured. The new tools need tether-browser 0.5.0 (npm install -g tether-browser).

version.approval_notes:
Tether is a developer tool: it lets a coding agent the user runs on their own computer (Claude Code, Codex and others) operate browser tabs the user explicitly shares. It does nothing until it is connected to its local program from the open source repository (npm install -g tether-browser, then tether setup). Source: https://github.com/udaysinh-git/tether; build with npm install && npm run build, the Firefox build is dist/firefox; the source is not minified or bundled.

New permission in this version, webRequestFilterResponse: used in extension/background.js to read the response bodies of fetch and XHR requests made by tabs the user shared, for the agent's network log (the network_request tool), and to hold a shared page's first bytes for at most 0.3 seconds until the console hook is injected, so console output from the start of a page load is not lost. The stream is passed through unchanged.

Running user code: the run_js tool, saved scripts and watchers run JavaScript the user's own agent supplies only through the userScripts API (userScripts.execute and userScripts.register), behind the optional userScripts permission the user grants in Tether's settings. There is no eval or Function constructor in the extension. Code comes from the local Tether program on the user's machine, never from a web server, and runs only in tabs the user shared or approved, with an on-page status panel showing Pause and Stop.

nativeMessaging: Firefox upgrades ws://127.0.0.1 to wss://, which cannot reach a local server, so Tether talks to its local program through a native messaging bridge. webRequestBlocking: lifts a page's Content Security Policy only on tabs the user shared, so the user's agent can work there. No data is collected or sent to the developer.
